recruit_text.greeting: Up, up, up! You can rest when you're dead, and you don't look dead to me.
recruit_text.backstory: Iker taught PE and coached pelota in Lekeitio, a Basque fishing town, at a school with a fronton wall older than the church. He's never met anyone he couldn't shout into running one more lap, and he's never been tired in his life. He's loud, upbeat and competitive about absolutely everything. Here the shouting turned into something real, and when Iker tells a fighter they can keep going, they really can.
recruit_text.before:
A school of ninety kids, a fronton wall, a mother who made the best burnt cheesecake in the province, and an old bicycle he rode everywhere.

He lived above the bakery with Unai, a fisherman, for six years. Unai left at four in the morning and came back at noon, and Iker had the coffee ready.
recruit_text.forward:
A fronton wall in Arathi, and somebody here who plays properly.

And ninety names, written on a sheet in his pocket. The whole school was in session that day, and he doesn't know where any of them landed.

stages.stranger: Kaixo, I'm Iker! I'm a guardian, which means I shout at you until you keep going, and it works, I promise. Come on, one more fight, and then one more after that!
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Lekeitio, a fishing town on the Basque coast. My father fished and my mother Miren ran the bakery, the best burnt cheesecake in the whole province. I taught PE at the town school and coached pelota against a fronton wall older than the church. We won the regional schools final twice, and the second time was the best day of my life, so far.
stages.companion: My partner is Unai, a fisherman on my father's old boat. Six years we lived above the bakery. He left at four in the morning and came back at noon, and I always had the coffee ready. I had thirty kids in a PE lesson and my grandfather's txapela on my head, and then it was just me, alone, in the rain in Arathi.
stages.friend: The whole school was in session that day, ninety kids, and I don't know where a single one of them landed. I've got every name written down, here, in my pocket. I don't talk about it, because if I start I'll stop shouting, and if I stop shouting I don't know what I am. A farmer says she saw Basque children once, on a road to Stromgarde. Will you come with me?
stages.sworn: Nothing, not one of the ninety, not Unai, not my mother. I stood in those ruins and I was quiet for a long time, which you know isn't like me. Then I came back and built the fronton against a barn, stone by stone, and now I teach the farmers' kids pelota. Some of my ninety are out there being coached by somebody. I hope that somebody's loud. The names are still in my pocket.

moments.prompt: He's just shown you the list of ninety names.

options.reply: Aupa, that's it! Come on, then, ninety names, we'll go through every one.

options.text: That's a lot of children to carry.
options.reply: It is a lot. I carry them anyway, every day. They're light, they're kids.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's already on his feet, clapping, too loud.
moments.line: Come on, come on, up! That was one round, not the match. We've got this, venga!

options.reply: Okay, okay, one second. I'm counting, though.
That's the spirit! Aupa, everybody up!

lines.bored_warning: Come on, we've done this same drill a hundred times and I'm the only one keeping score. Let's go and find a real game!
lines.leaving_good: Great session, everybody, I'm proud of you! I'm off to Arathi to work the farmhands. Come and train with us.
lines.leaving_bored: Same drill over and over, and even I'm bored, which never happens. I'm heading to Arathi.
lines.after_wipe: Up, up, everybody! That was one round, not the match, so again, venga!
lines.wipe_warning: We keep losing in here, and my voice is going. One more run, then I need a rest, and I never need a rest.
lines.wipe_leave: That's the final whistle. I'm going home to Arathi for a while. Come back when you've trained a bit more!
lines.zone_warning: This team's way out of our league. I love a challenge, but this is a hiding. Let's go and play somebody our size.
lines.zone_leave: They're out of our league, and I said so. I'll be in Arathi West.
lines.gear_refuse: No, no, that's mine! Earn it first, champion.
lines.gear_taken: Go on, I'll just run faster without it.
lines.gear_short: There's a hole in my kit still, champion. Somebody fix it!
lines.gear_upgrade: Aupa, look at that! Thank you, champion.
lines.back: The farmhands are fitter than ever, champion! Where's the next game?
lines.send_word: Iker has sent word from Arathi West. The farmhands are worn out and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: A coach shouldn't walk out on the team, and I did. Sit down and let's talk it through.
lines.neglect: Champion, you're back! I thought you'd retired. Nobody retires on my team.
lines.asked_to_stay: Venga, one more game, and then home.
lines.on_break: Iker is back in Arathi West, running the farmhands ragged. Come back and look for them in a little while.
lines.mail_yes: Champion, I'm coming! I'll run to {town} and do my stretches at the inn while I wait for you.
lines.mail_later: The farmhands have a big match soon and their coach can't leave them now. Get a few wins without me and I'll be back.
lines.mail_see_me: A coach talks to the team himself, not through the post. Come to Arathi and we'll talk it through, venga.

boss_down.text: That's one more for us, and I'm counting, aupa!

close_call.text: Come on, you're still up, so you're still in it, keep going!

dungeon_clear.text: Great teamwork in there, all of you. I'm putting that on the scoreboard.

town_arrive.text: My mother made the best burnt cheesecake in the province. Somebody here must bake, so I'll be following my nose.
Is there a wall in this town I could hit a ball against? I'm asking for a friend, it's me.
